newsitem.title: MEXICO: Swine fever strikes in Mexico's Puebla state.
newsitem.headline: Swine fever strikes in Mexico's Puebla state.

text.p: Swine fever has broken out in the northern part of the central Mexican state of Puebla, reported state-owned news agency Notimex.

Jose Luis Varela, an official with the state Agriculture Ministry, told Notimex that 80 pigs in the Sierra Norte part of the state were detected as having the disease. They were culled last week to prevent the disease spreading, he added.
Varela said health authorities had established a vigilance zone in the region in a bid to confine the disease with 16 inspection centers set up on roads leading out of the region.
Around 120 hog farms operate in the region with an estimated population of 1.5 million, he added.
State Agriculture Ministry spokesmen were not immediately to confirm the report.
